name: The Artillery Bulwark
summary: A low, wide round bulwark of sandstone with a gun platform level with the walks, a thick parapet ring, a ring of gunports at its base, and a bombard aimed out through its embrasure.
description: By the middle of the century the Burgundians were building for guns rather than against ladders. The bulwark is a squat round tower as wide as a house, its thick wall rising only to the level of the walks, so that its flat top becomes a gun platform. A parapet ring nearly a metre thick protects the gunners; a single wide embrasure faces the approach, with a bombard on its timber bed laid in it and its stone shot stacked beside. Lower down, five gunports pierce the base for hand-cannon that sweep the ditch. The walks run straight onto the platform through gaps in the parapet on either side.
build: Cell: 12.1 × 12.1 m (±6.05), no floor slab; the wall on the south edge, the bailey open to the north.

Drum: dressed sandstone, sixteen flats (circumradius 3.40 m, apothem 3.34 m), turned so a flat faces south, centred (0, −2.27) so the south flat lies on the walls' face line 0.45 m in from the cell edge; solid from the ground to the platform at 4.00 m, level with the walks.
Platform: a flagged disc r 2.45 m, 0.02 m, on the drum top.

Parapet ring: one sandstone block per flat, 0.84 m thick (radius 2.53 … 3.37), 4.00–5.00 m, alternate blocks 0.03 m higher; the four blocks facing 202.5°, 225°, 315° and 337.5° are left out where the walks come in.
Embrasure: the south block cut down to a sill 0.40 m high (4.00–4.40 m).
Gunports: five soot ports 0.30 × 0.30 m at 0.60–0.90 m on the flats facing 225°–315°.

Bombard: an oak bed 0.70 × 1.80 × 0.30 m at (0, −3.37) on the platform; an iron chamber r 0.20 m and bore r 0.30 m, 1.20 m long, along y with the muzzle south in the embrasure; two iron hoops; three stone balls r 0.20 m beside it.

Wall runs: the Late wall section (sandstone 1.60 m, face 0.45 m in, walk 4.00 m, brick frieze, corbels, parapet out to d 0.05, merlons to 5.20 m, timber walk) from each cell edge to x ±2.60, a keyhole gun-loop in each at x ±4.45.
sockets: Gun platform: 4.00 m, level with the walks, entered through the parapet gaps from both
Embrasure: south, sill at 4.40 m, the bombard laid in it
Gunports: five in the drum's base; keyhole gun-loops: one per run

materials.name: Dressed sandstone
materials.notes: Drum, parapet ring, runs; flagstones in vellum_faint.

gameplay: The platform is the Late wall's gun post: the bombard covers the approach, handgunners the base.
The walks run straight onto the platform, so guards can reinforce it from either side.
